messages.subject_clean: Broken parallelism Re: Miscellaneous usability questions
messages.body_plain:
On Thu, Jul 7, 2016 at 2:23 PM, Ed Merkle <ecme...@gmail.com> wrote:
> As I think about it more, I think the slowdown comes from summarizing the
> extra samples. First, runjags calculates posterior means/sds/etc using all
> samples drawn. Second, blavaan calculates log-likelihoods for each sample
> drawn. Some if (maybe all) of these calculations are not parallel, which
> partly explains the time increase.

Does blavaan do any of those calculations with burnin samples? (I
don't think anything needs to be done, they can be discarded as soon
as they're generated.) If not, then perhaps one work around for
parallelizing difficult models is to simply increase the burnin
substantially.

--
gwern
http://www.gwern.net

messages.body_plain:
The burnin samples never make it out of JAGS, so you could indeed use large burnin and then summarize fewer samples following burnin. I also just wrote some code that uses mclapply() for the posterior summaries, so this should also speed things up a bit.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Can I get 90% HPD?
messages.body_plain:
Seongho,

There is not currently a way to automatically obtain an HPD other than 95%. I will add this functionality soon.

For now, you should be able to do this (assuming your fitted model is "fit" and that the coda package is loaded):

HPDinterval(fit@external$runjags$mcmc, .9)

But the parameter names there will not match the names from summary(). So it is not optimal.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Error possibly a result of R 3.3.0
messages.subject_clean: Error possibly a result of R 3.3.0
messages.body_plain:
I recently set "auto" to be the default convergence option. I am not entirely happy with auto convergence because it takes a really long time (and, at least for exploratory modeling, we can often get by with fewer iterations). So I might switch the default back to "manual". Regardless, the functionality is there.

Ed

>
> Ed
